pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Introduce the Spring Boot RealWorld Example App, explaining its purpose as a demonstration of a production-grade backend implementation following the RealWorld specification with dual REST and GraphQL APIs

pages.title: Architecture & Design Patterns
pages.purpose: Explain the high-level architectural decisions including Domain-Driven Design, CQRS pattern, and the four-layer architecture that structures the application

pages.title: Domain-Driven Design (DDD)
pages.purpose: Detail how DDD principles are applied to separate the core business logic from infrastructure concerns, with the domain layer remaining consistent regardless of API adapter (REST or GraphQL)

pages.title: Layered Architecture
pages.purpose: Document the four architectural layers (API, Application, Core, Infrastructure) and their responsibilities, showing how separation of concerns is maintained

page_notes.content: Make sure to unpack the middleware

pages.title: API Layer
pages.purpose: Introduce the dual API approach, explaining how both REST and GraphQL APIs expose the same underlying domain model through different adapters

pages.title: REST API
pages.purpose: Document the RESTful API implementation using Spring MVC, including endpoint structure, request/response formats, and adherence to the RealWorld API specification

pages.title: Articles REST Endpoints
pages.purpose: Detail all article-related REST endpoints including creation, retrieval, updating, deletion, favoriting, and querying with filters and pagination

pages.title: Users REST Endpoints
pages.purpose: Document user registration, login, profile management, and follow/unfollow functionality through REST endpoints

pages.title: Comments REST Endpoints
pages.purpose: Explain comment creation, retrieval, and deletion endpoints, including authorization rules for comment management

pages.title: GraphQL API
pages.purpose: Document the GraphQL API implementation using Netflix DGS framework, including schema definition, queries, mutations, and pagination

pages.title: GraphQL Schema
pages.purpose: Present the complete GraphQL schema including types, queries, mutations, and input types, explaining the design decisions and how it maps to the domain model

pages.title: GraphQL Mutations
pages.purpose: Detail GraphQL mutations for user management and article operations, showing how they integrate with the command services layer

pages.title: GraphQL Queries and Data Fetchers
pages.purpose: Explain GraphQL query implementation including data fetchers, cursor-based pagination, and data enrichment with user context

pages.title: GraphQL Error Handling
pages.purpose: Document custom exception handling in GraphQL including authentication errors, validation errors, and error response formatting

pages.title: Security & Authentication
pages.purpose: Explain the security architecture including Spring Security configuration, JWT-based authentication, and authorization mechanisms

pages.title: Security Configuration
pages.purpose: Detail the Spring Security setup including CORS configuration, endpoint authorization rules, and stateless session management

pages.title: JWT Authentication
pages.purpose: Explain JWT token generation, validation, and the custom JwtTokenFilter that processes authentication on each request

pages.title: Password Encoding
pages.purpose: Document the use of BCrypt for secure password hashing and the encryption service abstraction

pages.title: Application Layer
pages.purpose: Describe the application services layer that orchestrates business operations and serves as the boundary between API and domain layers

pages.title: Command Services
pages.purpose: Detail command services that handle write operations including validation, authorization checks, and coordination with domain entities

pages.title: Query Services
pages.purpose: Explain query services that optimize read operations, perform data enrichment, and transform domain entities into DTOs

pages.title: Data Persistence
pages.purpose: Document the persistence layer including database schema, MyBatis implementation, and the Data Mapper pattern

pages.title: Database Schema
pages.purpose: Present the complete database schema including all tables, relationships, and design rationale for the social blogging platform

pages.title: MyBatis Data Mapper
pages.purpose: Explain the MyBatis implementation including XML mapper configurations, the Data Mapper pattern, and SQL query organization

pages.title: Repository Layer
pages.purpose: Document repository interfaces and implementations, transaction management, and the separation between command and query repositories

pages.title: Database Migrations
pages.purpose: Explain Flyway migration setup and the versioned migration strategy for schema evolution

pages.title: Build & Development
pages.purpose: Cover the build system, development tools, code quality enforcement, and dependency management

pages.title: Gradle Build Configuration
pages.purpose: Detail the Gradle build setup including dependencies, plugins (Spring Boot, DGS codegen, Spotless), and custom tasks

pages.title: Gradle Wrapper
pages.purpose: Explain the Gradle Wrapper mechanism that ensures consistent build environments across different systems

pages.title: Development Workflow
pages.purpose: Document local development setup, running the application, database configuration, and code formatting with Spotless

pages.title: Testing Strategy
pages.purpose: Explain the comprehensive testing approach including unit tests, integration tests, API tests, and the test infrastructure

pages.title: Deployment
pages.purpose: Cover deployment options including local execution, Docker containerization, and CI/CD pipeline

pages.title: Local Deployment
pages.purpose: Explain how to run the application locally using Gradle, including SQLite database setup and configuration

pages.title: Docker Deployment
pages.purpose: Document Docker image creation using Spring Boot's bootBuildImage and container execution

pages.title: CI/CD Pipeline
pages.purpose: Detail the GitHub Actions workflow for continuous integration including automated testing and build verification
